text:
The statute is most likely constitutional, with no equal protection violation. The 20% vote test is an objective measure of electoral support, and the state has a legitimate interest in limiting the ballot to candidates with a demonstrated base, so the party/non-party distinction is justified. The 7% petition is comparable to the 5% requirement upheld in *Jenness v. Fortson*, and the 180-day circulation period matches the party deadline, so the burden is modest under *Anderson-Burdick*.

CONFIDENCE: 62
